question: What is another common name for hospital-acquired infections?
explanation: Nosocomial infections is the medical term used specifically for infections picked up by a patient while admitted inside a healthcare facility. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h1)

question: When do symptoms of a true hospital-acquired infection typically begin to show?

options.B: Within the first two hours of arrival
options.D: Before the patient enters the ward

explanation: The 48-hour window helps clinicians confirm that the patient caught the germ inside the hospital rather than carrying it in from the community. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h1)

question: Which type of nosocomial infection is most directly linked to the use of an indwelling urethral tube?
explanation: Any infection of the urinary tract related to a catheter in place is classified specifically as a CAUTI. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h2)

question: What time frame defines a surgical site infection after an operation?

options.A: Only while the patient is sleeping
options.D: After exactly six months of healing

explanation: An infection is classified as a surgical site infection if it develops around the incision within thirty days after the procedure. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h2)

question: What is the single most common route for spreading hospital-acquired infections?

options.A: Direct insect bites from house flies
options.C: Contact transmission via hands or equipment
options.D: Inhaling outdoor dust storms near wards

explanation: Healthcare workers moving from patient to patient with unwashed hands remain the leading pathway for spreading hospital germs. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h3)

question: Why do hospital pathogens pose a greater treatment challenge than community strains?

options.A: They are completely invisible to standard microscopes
options.B: They multiply exclusively at freezing temperatures
options.C: They frequently show resistance to common antibiotics
options.D: They can only survive inside metal surgical trays

explanation: Constant exposure to drugs in hospitals helps select for hardy, resistant bacterial strains that standard medications cannot easily kill. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h3)

question: Which physiological feature makes newborn babies especially prone to hospital infections?

options.A: Immature immune systems and fragile skin barriers
options.B: An excessive amount of natural body fat
options.C: Higher than normal adult body temperature
options.D: A complete absence of blood circulation

explanation: Newborns have not yet developed fully mature immune defenses, making it easy for hospital bacteria to invade through their delicate skin. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h4)

question: Which postpartum patient faces the highest risk for developing a direct surgical site infection?

options.A: A mother who experienced a spontaneous birth
options.B: A healthy mother discharged after six hours
options.C: An antenatal client waiting for her scan
options.D: A mother recovering from a caesarean section

explanation: Surgical incisions break the protective skin barrier, creating a primary entry route for pathogens compared to an intact perineum after normal birth. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of hospital infection surveillance systems?

options.A: To collect and analyze data for detecting outbreaks
options.B: To punish staff members who make clinical mistakes
options.C: To calculate daily patient feeding budgets
options.D: To design new advertisements for the maternity wing

explanation: Surveillance is designed to track infection trends and spot unusual clusters of disease early so action can be taken. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a helpful clinical sign of infection for a midwife to document and report?

options.A: Normal baseline temperature and pink lochia
options.B: Foul-smelling lochia and lower abdominal pain
options.C: Purulent discharge oozing from a C-section wound
options.D: Persistent unexplained fever on the third day

explanation: Normal vital signs and standard healing processes do not indicate an infection and require no special reporting. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h5)

question: What is considered the single most effective measure for preventing hospital-acquired infections?
explanation: Cleaning hands before and after touching patients stops germs from transferring between beds and is the baseline of infection control. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h6)

question: Why is proper waste segregation using color-coded bins important in a maternity ward?

options.A: It helps patients identify which doctor is on duty
options.B: It ensures that waste decomposes faster in the sun
options.C: It prevents accidental needle-stick injuries and contamination
options.D: It lowers the monthly electricity bill for the hospital

explanation: Separating sharps and infectious waste protects both healthcare workers and sanitation staff from accidental injury and dangerous exposure. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h6)
